description: The decision precedence table as data. Each row is one log shape and the decision every conforming implementation must reach; the corpus test reads this file, so a disagreement is a failure rather than a coincidence.

rows.why: One claim, reported, with nothing failing, is the success case.
A failed assertion is the strongest disproof and outranks everything below it.

Kani attributes a check to the function owning its source line, so an assertion in a routine the harness calls is reported inside the harness's block under that routine's name. The block printed FAILED, so the run disproved something the claim depends on; reading only the harness's own checks would call it verified.

Kani printed FAILED and reconciled a failure count, so a failure exists; none of the checks this decision can attribute carries it. Ownership explains whose failure it was, not whether the run succeeded, so the verdict decides it a counterexample rather than verified.

CBMC printed the failed assertion without naming an owner, so the block it appears in is the harness it was checked for. A failure the block reported denies the claim whether or not a routine is named beside it.
A timeout elsewhere cannot soften a counterexample that was already found.
A timeout is a resource limit, which VO-11b ranks above an undecided check.
An unwinding failure says the bound was too small, not that the property is false.

The failing assertion was generated for a loop in a routine the harness called, not for the harness's own. Kani still reported a bound that was too small, and VO-11b ranks that as resource exhaustion wherever it appears; reading only the harness's own unwinding checks would let the block's FAILED verdict call it a counterexample.
Kani named a construct it cannot model, so the gap is the tool's, not the solver's.
Nothing names a missing capability, so the solver simply did not decide.
A failed unsupported_construct check is a capability gap, not a disproof.
DL-09: a manifest claim with no result in the log was skipped.
Any unreported claim makes the run incomplete, however well the reported one did.
A control that failed exactly the property it declares is the run working as designed.

A control that verified means the seeded fault was not exercised. VO-11b ranks outcomes over claim harnesses only, so the run itself still reads verified; the control's `accepted` status is the evidence, and the gate blocks on `control-some-accepted`.
A mis-targeted control does not disprove the claim; the record reports it as rejected-otherwise and the gate blocks on that reason.
Kani's verdict note says the panic was the expected one, so its failed assertion is the claim.
The certified panic explains the unreachable check after it; the claim is still the panic the manifest asked for.
Without the note the harness failed for some other reason, which the manifest may not excuse.
A harness that assumed its own precondition away proved nothing, so an unreachable witness must not read as verified.
kani list output carries no verdict, so it cannot be decided from.
VO-11b: a harness without a role is a structural error.
